blocking.issue: The Token Budget reservation in P8 is not an upper bound, so SM-10 still cannot be verified. When a client omits max_tokens, P8 reserves 'a Policy default cap', but nothing requires the gateway to send that cap upstream. OpenAI and Gemini then generate up to the model maximum, so actual usage can exceed the reservation without limit. The admission rule is also unstated. If a request is admitted whenever charged usage is below B, rather than only when the remaining budget covers the whole reservation, 200 x 4,096 tokens (82% of B) can be in flight past the limit. Even with atomic reservations, the remaining overshoot comes from prompt-token estimation error multiplied by prompt size and concurrency. Anthropic has no public tokenizer, and Opus 4.7+ produces about 30% more tokens for the same text (ai-gateways.md section 3.1). SM-10 fixes none of these inputs, and its mock provider decides what usage it reports, so the 1% figure can be passed or failed at will.
blocking.evidence: P8: "A Token Budget reserves estimated prompt tokens plus `max_tokens` (or a Policy default cap) at admission and settles with authoritative provider-reported usage". SM-10: "Mock provider; budget B = 1,000,000 tokens, 200 concurrent streams, `max_tokens` = 4,096, reservations per P8 | 1% of B or less (hypothesis)". Research: "Anthropic: Claude Opus 4.7 and later use a newer tokenizer that produces about 30% more tokens for the same text" and "No public tokenizer; POST /v1/messages/count_tokens (free, estimate)" (ai-gateways.md sections 3 and 3.1).
blocking.fix: In P8, replace "(or a Policy default cap)" with "(a Policy default cap, written into the upstream request's output-token limit when the client omits one)" and add "admission requires the remaining budget to cover the full reservation". Keep P8 at two sentences, for example by moving the degraded-state clause to Success metrics. In SM-10's measurement column, fix the mock: "2,000-token prompts; the mock reports prompt usage 2% above the gateway estimate and drops usage on 5% of streams". State the bound as "overshoot is at most the sum of per-stream estimate error, and 1% of B or less (hypothesis)". Alternatively, keep the 1% figure and name the tokenizer-accuracy assumption it depends on.

blocking.issue: P2 and P4 are absolute, and the System Overview contradicts them for Control-mode Clusters. A new Node needs Ruralz Control to enroll and to receive its first Revision. The System Overview says a Node with no Last-Known-Good stays not ready, and it lists enrollment as lost while Ruralz Control is unreachable. So when Ruralz Control is down or Raft quorum is lost, a rescheduled Kubernetes pod with an empty RURALZ_DATA_DIR, or any autoscaled replacement, cannot serve traffic. Capacity lost during a control-plane incident cannot be replaced. That contradicts "never a runtime dependency" and "Nodes are disposable". Every design document inherits these principles, so the High availability and Deployment topologies documents would violate them however they are designed.
blocking.evidence: P2: "Ruralz Control adds value and is never a runtime dependency." P4: "Nodes are disposable | ... join or leave a Cluster without coordinating with other Nodes. Enrollment is one-time and off the request path (file and OCI mode need none)". System Overview: "A new Node with no Last-Known-Good stays not ready (seeding: OQ-system-overview-12...)" and failure table "Ruralz Control unreachable or Raft quorum lost | Management: Rollouts, Ruralz Console, Drift, enrollment".
blocking.fix: Rewrite P2's second sentence: "Ruralz Control is never on the serving path of an enrolled Node; in Control mode, adding a Node needs Ruralz Control for enrollment and a first Revision unless the Node is seeded from an OCI-published Last-Known-Good (OQ-system-overview-12)." In P4, add "in Control mode, scale-out during a Ruralz Control outage is bounded by OQ-system-overview-12", or cross-reference that open question from this document's Open questions.

non_blocking.suggestion: The harness passed an empty list of previous blocking items, but the prior L1 verdict on disk had L1-1 to L1-9. All nine were checked against this revision and are resolved: P3 bound and rename, P4 durable state and enrollment, P8 reservation and settlement, SM-4/SM-5/SM-9 measurement conditions, P6 limits and aggregate cap, P7 per-protocol Phase mapping, Managed cloud tenancy and exit, Kong attribution, and P1 scoping.

Name every default the System Overview already fixes: the `ai.token-budget` default is `failureMode: closed`, and Plugin traps default to `closed`. Otherwise a reader may treat Token Budgets as Rate Limits and assume they fail open.

State the JWT algorithm (for example ES256 with a cached JWKS) and whether the listener is plaintext or TLS. Signature verification cost and TLS record processing move p50 by tens of microseconds, which is significant against a 150 µs target.

The tenancy rule dedicates `ruralz-control` and the Control Store per customer, but says nothing about the State Store or Nodes that Revington runs. Either dedicate them per customer too, or state that sharing relies on public State Store key-prefix and ACL settings. Otherwise shared runtime state implies a multi-tenant feature with no milestone.

"One feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build": clarify that the FIPS build keeps every feature but configuration validation rejects non-approved algorithm choices (for example X25519 key exchange or ChaCha20-Poly1305 cipher suites), so the claim stays literally true.

When per-Node Rate Limit shares come from a Node count that Ruralz Control publishes, shares are stale during scale-out and over-admit locally for one publication interval. Note that GCRA in the State Store remains the global bound, and point to Scalability and distributed state for the accuracy figure.
